title: CICIoT2023 — early-detectability map: which attack types are learnable-early, on which axis, and does the data support the honest test
basis: packet-2 behavioural features (no MAC/IP as features); device identity only builds the split; XGBoost seed42 n_jobs1; threshold=1% FPR on seen; multi-partition sweep; TRUE device holdout (attack+benign of the held device in test only).

categories.honest_frame: victim-disjoint (train on some victim devices, test on unseen victims)
categories.result: FAILS to transfer. Seen-device AUC 0.99 / FPR 1% -> unseen-device AUC median 0.66 (3/10 partitions at chance), FPR 10-99% (median 83%). Flat across packet-2/20/full-flow (fingerprinting, not earliness).

categories.honest_frame: attacker-disjoint (train on some scanner sources, test on unseen scanners)
categories.note: scanners identified by fan-out (>=50 distinct dst IPs), not distinct src (avoids counting responders). PingSweep skipped (<2 scanners at fanout>=50). HostDiscovery is 46% single-packet (packet-2 thin).
categories.result: PARTIALLY transfers. Seen AUC 0.97-0.99 / FPR 1% -> unseen-scanner AUC 0.67-0.82 (PortScan 0.82, HostDiscovery 0.76, VulnScan 0.75, OSScan 0.66), FPR 5-13%. Ports carry scan signal (OSScan -> chance 0.52 without ports; others hold).
categories.verdict: partially generalizes to unseen scanners (far better than floods, still degraded)

categories.honest_frame: host/service-disjoint (train on some target hosts, test on unseen hosts)
categories.note: each concentrates on a single target host (0-1 non-infra victim at 5%), so a host-disjoint split is structurally impossible. BrowserHijacking is the one exception (3 Raspberry-Pi camera hosts) but they are near-identical device types.
categories.result: UNTESTABLE for generalization on this data (single target). That the data cannot support the honest test is itself a finding.
categories.verdict: not measurable here (single target per class)

categories.honest_frame: attacker-disjoint / behaviour-signature (victim identity is secondary; the attacker inserts itself)
categories.data_supports_frame: unknown (not yet censused on the attacker/fan-out axis)
categories.note: the dst-victim counts (3 each) are the WRONG axis for this category; needs an attacker/behaviour census like recon before a test.
2 target hosts at 5% (bare minimum, 1 train / 1 test) - as fragile as greeth.
categories.result: not run (too thin to be meaningful alone)

headline: The packet-2 fingerprinting limit is ATTACK-TYPE-DEPENDENT, not universal. Floods fingerprint the victim and fail to transfer (AUC 0.66, FPR 10-99%). Recon/scans partially transfer to unseen scanners (AUC 0.67-0.82, FPR 5-13%). Web/brute attacks are single-target so the honest test is not even constructible on this data (a dataset-limitation finding). MITM/spoofing need an attacker-axis census not yet done.
caveats: One dataset (CICIoT2023), one model class (XGBoost), packet-2 features, TCP/UDP only.
Small, overlapping device pools (~16 victims, 13 scanners) - fragile splits, reported as ranges over partitions.
identity-fingerprint vs device-type shift cannot be fully separated without device-type labels.
recon per-file labels include benign background; attack flows restricted to scanner-source flows to reduce it.
